items.summary: People meet each other less than they did twenty years ago, and the reason is not that they stopped liking each other. After reading this you can explain the forces behind it, tell loneliness apart from solitude, plan shared time that people actually attend, and keep a friendship alive across distance and full calendars.
items.title: Why People Are Spending Less Time Together

items.summary: Working from another country is now possible for tens of millions of people, but it is governed by visa rules, tax rules and the cost of daily life. After reading this you can tell a genuine digital nomad from a tourist working online, check what you must do before you move, and pick a city that fits your work and your budget.
items.title: Digital Nomads: Working From Anywhere

items.summary: Moving to a new country changes small things before big ones: greetings, meals, punctuality, silence. After reading this you can name what is surprising you, tell a personal habit from a local rule, and handle the first weeks without assuming that your way is the correct one.
items.title: Culture Shock: Things That Surprise People Abroad

items.summary: English is one language with many accents, and most of the differences you meet are regular rather than wrong. After reading this you can recognise British, American, Australian, Indian and Singapore English by their vocabulary and grammar, understand why the differences exist, and choose the variety that fits your listener.
items.title: Why English Is Different Around the World
